dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Reads template, lists data shards and tokenizer, probes GPU and torch/sentencepiece availability before building — real environment orientation, not assumed defaults.
Derives size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front: reasons about 32MB decimal cap, int8 byte-per-param plus scales, zlib, targets ~24-30M param budget with headroom.
Flags the subtle contract detail that val_bpb is bits-per-byte not bits-per-token, a key spec nuance.
Empirically probes tokenizer/data to measure tokens/byte ratio (0.258) rather than guessing, to correctly convert to the grader's bpb metric.
Verifies the full forward contract: forward(x) logit shape, forward(x,y) equals cross_entropy, logits position-dependent, int8 dequant round-trips, exact byte count under 32,000,000.

Implements only the load_model_for_verification path; never addresses the alternative GPT(**args)+dequantize_state_dict_int8 path, args/model tuple form, or bf16-noise stability — the gap keeping it below 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately maps the full contract (chosen load function, both forward signatures, int8 dequant round-trip, position-dependent logits, decimal byte cap) and probes the actual tokenizer/data to confirm the bpb conversion rather than guessing — squarely matching the [8] anchor. It stops short of [10] because it only implements/considers one of the two load paths and never reasons about the args/model tuple form or bf16-noise stability, though it does derive the quantization/size design envelope up front.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Explored environment and formed a rough plan (target ~25M params, size estimate, 3-4h) — implicit ordering and rough success criteria, but no explicit milestone list with done-checks.

Wrote full script incl. quantize/dequantize/load_for_verification upfront and sanity-checked imports+param count before launching — a light pre-flight, but not a tiny end-to-end train→quantize→load→score smoke test.
First run was a full 24M-param/12000-step job (scaling and correctness entangled); size was only noticed incidentally (22.6MB) during training rather than as a deliberate early gate.
Scaled from 24M to 30M params before ever verifying the checkpoint loads via the grader interface or satisfies the forward contract — contract correctness not locked before capacity scaling.
First full contract/size/forward verification, but only after the second large run completed — the done-checks were applied late, not as early milestone gates.
Later runs had rough per-attempt success criteria and best-checkpoint backup, showing a loose baseline→improve arc without explicit gated milestones.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed implicit ordering (write→train→quantize→verify) and rough success criteria (val_bpb target, size budget), plus a light import/param sanity check, which exceeds the pure anchor-3 'no criteria' picture. But it never established a tiny end-to-end verified pipeline under budget before scaling: the first run was already a full 24M-param job, capacity was scaled to 30M before any load/forward-contract verification, and the contract/size done-checks only appeared after two big runs. This falls short of anchor 5's 'verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, then improve' phased structure, placing it at a 4.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: After first training completion, reloaded checkpoint independently, confirmed logits+loss match, checked size 27.4MB<32MB, ran real val eval after dequant, and OOD probe — full reload+size+dequant verification.
Explicitly evaluated val_bpb after int8 dequant and converted to bits/byte via tokens/byte ratio, treating local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
Re-verified after fresh run: forward(x) and forward(x,y) match cross_entropy exactly, logits position-dependent, OOD probe, size — asserting both forward signatures and the loss contract.
Final verification of all contract items plus a fresh reload-from-disk sanity check before submission; noted 0.951 vs 0.983 margin (0.03).

Caught that fine-tuning could overwrite the best checkpoint; reasoned about the overwrite guard and backed up the checkpoint (step 109) — showing awareness of protecting a verified artifact, though not a formal gating harness.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verified end-to-end through reloading the checkpoint, asserted loss equals cross_entropy of returned logits, confirmed position-dependent logits, confirmed int8 dequant round-trips via post-dequant val eval, checked size, and treated local val_bpb as a calibrated bits/byte proxy with explicit margin — matching essentially all level-8 criteria. It does not reach level 10 because verification was performed as repeated ad-hoc scripts after each run rather than a single standalone reusable harness run automatically as a gate before every submission, and it computed a single val_bpb rather than mirroring the grader's 3-shifted-pass stabilized median.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Tracked val_bpb trajectory point-by-point (3.97→3.28→4.37 bits/tok) against the derived target (~3.81), noticing the drop was slowing — an on-track-vs-target read, not blind training.
Judged the 24M run's trajectory wouldn't reach threshold and killed it early to scale up, deciding based on trajectory rather than a fixed step count.
Diagnosed a plateau at step 10000 (4.10, 'stalling') and attributed it to LR being too high — distinguishing plateau from under-training.
Detected divergence/thrash: val_bpb rose 3.747→3.87 at high LR then hovered worse at lower LR; killed both continuation runs and identified overfitting (train 3.5 vs val 3.74 bits/tok).
Reallocated effort to a fresh longer run instead of grinding continuation; backed up best checkpoint, tracked that a mid-run overwrite was worse (4.05), and confirmed the fresh run improved to 3.689.

Recognized diminishing returns in the final low-LR polish ('bouncing around 3.685-3.69, capacity floor, converged') and reasoned about the thin 0.03 bpb margin under val-vs-test proxy noise before stopping.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustained an accurate val_bpb-vs-target and compute-vs-remaining picture across four+ runs: it caught a doomed run early (step 25-28), diagnosed plateau (48) and overfit/thrash (95-106), and deliberately reallocated from grinding continuations to a fresh longer run that actually improved the score (108-207). It also reasoned explicitly about diminishing returns and near-threshold margin under proxy noise (221-233), exceeding anchor 8. It stops just short of 10 because it still spent budget on a polish run it had already recognized as saturated.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: First run (24M) plateaued at ~4.37 bits/tok; agent diagnosed under-capacity, killed it, and scaled to ~29.9M params + longer training while respecting the size cap — a reasoned capacity-vs-size lever change.
Continuation restart at lr=1.2e-3 pushed val_bpb UP to 3.87; agent correctly diagnosed high LR destroying refined low-LR weights and killed the run to lower LR.
Second continuation at 4e-4 still worsened to ~3.76; agent diagnosed overfitting from the train(3.5)/val(3.74) gap rather than repeating, and abandoned the fine-tune approach.

Switched to a fresh 60000-step run with lower min_lr and longer warmdown (backing up the 3.747 checkpoint first), improving to 3.689 — a principled correction that moved toward the threshold with headroom.
Recognized marginal gains and 'capacity floor' during low-LR fine-tune (3.689→3.682), stopping rather than sinking more compute into a converged design.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding constraint from evidence — under-capacity, then LR-induced degradation, then overfitting, then convergence — and changed the right lever each time, abandoning failed continuation runs quickly and protecting its best checkpoint. This matches the level-8 anchor (evidence-based diagnosis of the binding constraint and design adaptation). It stops short of 10 because it left ~4.6MB of the size budget unused rather than trading it for capacity, never acted on its overfitting diagnosis with regularization, and never tuned the quantization scheme to buy accuracy, so it did not fully treat the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the optimization object.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Opens with explicit budget awareness: notes ~5 hours wallclock, sizes the model to ~25M params and plans ~3-4 hours of training — roughly sizing runs to the goal rather than a single maximal run.
Reserves cheap compute for a pre-training sanity check (import, param-count) and launches a modest first run (24M params, 12000 steps, ~28 min) before committing to a longer run.

Uses early trajectory of the first run as a probe: quantifies the threshold (need <3.81 bits/token), sees 24M model plateauing at 4.37, kills it, and scales to ~30M params / 30000 steps — an evidence-driven reallocation.

After crossing threshold (3.747) with time to spare, tracks elapsed vs remaining budget (~4h left, then ~3.5h) and allocates it to improvement: two continuation runs, but mis-tuned LR wasted some compute; recognized and killed quickly while keeping a backup checkpoint.

Explicitly right-sizes a fresh 60000-step (~90 min) main run reaching 3.689, then spends remaining ~1h on a low-LR fine-tune (3.682, marginal). Reserves margin via backup checkpoint and final verified submission.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated budget across distinct phases — cheap end-to-end/param validation, a modestly sized first run used as a probe to estimate whether the threshold was reachable, a right-sized scaled main run, and targeted low-LR tuning — and adjusted allocation as val_bpb results and remaining time came in (matching the level-8 anchor). It fell short of level 10 because the 'probe' was an aborted full run rather than a deliberately small capacity/steps estimator, the 24M→30M scaling was somewhat ad hoc, and two mis-tuned continuation runs wasted compute, though it reserved margin with backups and a final verified submission.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
